Going left would force the line onto number 5 before its turn. So the line goes down.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going left would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order); going right, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,6); going down would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So my guess (right from cell (3,4)) was wrong, so the line must go down.

Going right would force the line onto number 6 before its turn; going through the portal to (5,3) would leave both cell (4,3) and cell (6,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up.
Going right would leave both cell (1,2) and cell (3,2) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Cell (6,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
